content.title: About
content.content: Empanada, no meat is a traditional Spanish‑Latin American pastry made from a thin dough filled with vegetables, cheese and spices. The dough is usually prepared from wheat flour, water, oil and salt, while the filling may include spinach, corn, potato, bell pepper, onion and aromatic herbs.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “empanada” comes from the Spanish verb “empanar”, meaning “to wrap in dough”.
Different countries have their own typical fillings: Argentina often uses corn and cheese, Chile adds seafood, and Mexico favors black beans and cheese.
Traditionally the empanada is shaped like a half‑moon, but it can also be round, square or triangular.
Empanadas are commonly served at festivals, family gatherings and as street food.

items.title: Rich in vegetables
items.content: A vegetable‑based filling provides a spectrum of vitamins (C, A, folate) and antioxidants.

items.title: Low in saturated fat
items.content: The absence of meat and the use of plant‑based fats make this empanada more heart‑friendly.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Vegetables and whole‑grain dough support digestion and promote satiety.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Cheese and legumes in the filling add plant‑based protein useful for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: When made with whole‑grain flour, the empanada provides a steadier blood‑sugar response.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat flour dough can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Cheese in the filling may be problematic for those who cannot digest lactose.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Salted cheese and added salt can increase sodium intake, which is a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The combination of dough and cheese makes the empanada relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Empanadas are best served hot, either as a snack or a main dish. They are convenient to eat with hands, but can also be sliced and paired with sauces such as salsa, guacamole or a yogurt‑based dip.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked empanadas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag – they keep well for up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly to ensure the filling is hot throughout.
